meta.title: Overserved – How Far AI-Assisted Development Goes | LumiVerse
meta.description: A satirical AI tower-defense game – 7 worlds, 140 levels, 600+ generated art assets, built in three weeks – an honest test of how far AI dev goes.

en.title: Overserved
en.subtitle: A satirical AI-themed tower defense: you don't shoot users, you serve them. Seven markets, 140 levels, 600+ generated art assets, built in about three weeks – as an honest test of how far AI-assisted development actually goes.

showcase.alt: Overserved gameplay - the isometric serve funnel from Sign-Up to Exit, with generated decor and the tower palette
Campaign market select - seven worlds, each with its own Smarts, Privacy and Vibe lens
An Overserved story panel - generated comic art with the opening narration

stats.label: Generated art assets, every prompt logged
Levels, each tuned by a bot that played it
Devlog entries, published as it was built

closing.title: Want This Pointed at Your Backlog?
closing.body: The pipelines behind Overserved – reproducible generation, written-down invariants, bots that measure what matters – are the same ones we bring to client work. Go and play the result first.

sections.title: How Far Does It Actually Go?
sections.lede: A game is a brutal test: working code, hundreds of art assets, twenty hours of fun levels and jokes that land. So we built one.

items.title: The Setup
items.body:
One person, three weeks, 580 commits. A real game shipped to a real URL – not a prototype, not a demo reel. Campaign mode, endless survival, a meta-progression tree, a knowledge base, saved progress, and an Android build.

Every decision, dead end and revert written up publicly while it happened.

items.title: The Honest Answer
items.body:
Further than expected on volume – code, art and levels came fast enough that scope stopped being the constraint. Not as far on taste. The AI could tell whether a level was survivable; it could not tell whether it was boring.

The interesting work turned out to be building the tools that let a human judge quickly, then judging.

sections.title: Code, Art, Levels, Jokes
sections.lede: Four different kinds of output, four different pipelines – each one turned into a repeatable process rather than a lucky prompt.

items.title: The Game Itself
items.body:
Phaser 3 and TypeScript, around 17,000 lines across 54 modules: two-camera HUD, isometric projection maths, projectile ballistics with tile-ring blast falloff, wave generation, boss abilities, save system, procedural audio. A type-check gate has to pass before every single commit.

Game invariants written down as rules the AI must not break
Balance lives in data files, never in ad-hoc scene logic
Every hard-won gotcha recorded so it isn't relearned

items.title: 140 Unique Paths
items.body: Every level gets its own funnel, generated by a script and frozen into the build. Entrances rotate across all four edges, a minimum-corner count rises as you progress, and length is bounded to what that market can afford to defend. The build aborts if any level misses its floor.

items.title: 600+ Assets, One Pipeline
items.body:
Towers, users, bosses, decor, tiles, UI icons and comic panels – all generated, then background-removed by a segmentation model, trimmed to content, logged and installed. The prompt, seed, resolution and model for every generation sit in a JSON file in the repo, so any asset can be reproduced or reverted.

The whole process is written as a reusable skill, not a habit
Colour-keying dropped for AI segmentation – it stopped eating teal furniture
Four-directional characters derived from one flat image, for cents

items.title: Seven Worlds, Seven Rulesets
items.body: USA, Europe, China, Africa, Earth, Space and Rogue. Each market applies a lens that rewrites what a good answer is worth – Europe makes privacy king with a red-tape floor, China's firewall censors cheap answers. Same towers, completely different puzzle.

items.title: The Jokes
items.body: Satirical breaking-news interstitials between levels, taunts from thinly-veiled tech-titan bosses, and a chatbot tower that pops a different smug reply on every hit. Written to a tone spec, then filtered by a human for the ones that actually landed.

items.title: Sound Without a Sound Library
items.body: Music and effects are synthesized in code rather than sampled – menu theme, UI clicks, serve hits, explosions. Nothing to license, nothing to download, and it tunes like any other data file.

items.title: Runs on a Phone
items.body: Wrapped for Android with orientation locking and a splash screen, after a performance pass that found the frame budget going to a HUD redrawing itself sixty times a second – not to the game.

items.alt: Overserved main menu showing campaign, survival, R&D lab, AGI lab and knowledge base modes

sections.title: A Bot That Plays the Game
sections.lede: Difficulty tuning is game dev's slowest loop, so a headless autoplayer drives the real engine and reports how close it came to losing.

items.title: It Plays Properly
items.body: Not a dumb script. It places towers by marginal coverage using each tower's actual range, weights tiles toward the exit where leaks really happen, reads the market lens when choosing what to buy, banks currency, builds labs and spends on upgrades – because a real player does all of that, and a bot that doesn't will fail levels that are actually fine.

items.title: It Found Real Bugs
items.body: Running it across every level exposed problems no amount of staring at a spreadsheet would: a difficulty wall driven by damage-per-cost rather than raw damage, and bosses that leaked unserved because they trailed behind their own escort and the towers shot the escort instead.

items.title: Then It Designed Them
items.body: Once it could play well, hand-tuned difficulty knobs became noise. Level design was handed over: each wave grows until the bot barely survives it. All 140 levels are tuned by something that actually played them, not by a designer guessing.

sections.title: Where It Still Needed a Human
sections.lede: The failures are the useful part – every one is in the devlog, because a case study that lists only wins isn't worth reading.

items.title: Balanced Isn't the Same as Fun
items.body:
The bot proved every level was winnable. It could not tell that some of them were dull. Three deliberately overpowered towers went in and it never even noticed – the economy absorbed them. "Survivable" is measurable; "worth twenty minutes of your evening" is not.

A whole feature – per-stat tower upgrades – shipped and was deleted the same day. It worked perfectly and made the game worse to play.

items.title: Reverting Beats Re-Rolling
items.body:
Regenerating a cohesive set one asset at a time quietly destroys it – each render drifts in scale, perspective and framing until the collection stops matching itself. The tower set got measurably worse that way and was restored from git.

A whole world shipped as another world with a red filter over it. Flat colour isn't art direction, and only a person looking at it said so.

items.title: What That Actually Means for Client Work
items.body: The lesson isn't "AI builds games now." It's that generation is cheap and judgement is not, so the edge sits in the scaffolding around the generation: a logged, reproducible asset pipeline; invariants written down where they can't be forgotten; a bot that measures the thing you actually care about; and a human whose whole job is deciding what's good. Overserved is where we built and stress-tested that scaffolding – on our own time, on a project where a bad call costs nothing.

sections.title: Twenty-Two Entries, Failures Included
sections.lede: Notes from building it – what was tried, what broke, what it taught. A sample:

items.title: Jul 4
items.body: I stopped tuning the levels. I let the bot design them.

items.title: Jul 2
items.body: The bottleneck wasn't the game. It was the scoreboard.

items.title: Jun 25
items.body: My spreadsheet said the game was balanced. It couldn't tell me it was boring.

items.title: Jun 25
items.body: I made three overpowered towers. The bot didn't even notice.

items.title: Jun 24
items.body: One prompt line fixed 96 of my buildings.

items.title: Jun 23
items.body: I built a bot to play my game 140 times. It found a wall I couldn't see.

items.title: Jun 19
items.body: I got 4-direction characters out of a flat AI image for two cents each.

items.title: Jun 17
items.body: I built per-stat tower upgrades, then deleted them by dinner.

showcase.alt: Overserved u igri - izometrijski lijevak od prijave do izlaza, s generiranim ukrasima i paletom kula
Odabir tržišta u kampanji - sedam svjetova, svaki sa svojom lećom pameti, privatnosti i dojma
Strip-kadar iz priče Overserveda - generirana grafika s uvodnom naracijom

stats.label: Od praznog repozitorija do igrive igre

Zapisa u devlogu, objavljenih tijekom izrade

closing.title: Želite ovo usmjereno na svoj backlog?
closing.body: Pipelineovi iza Overserveda — ponovljivo generiranje, zapisana nepromjenjiva pravila, botovi koji mjere ono što je važno — isti su oni koje donosimo u rad s klijentima. Prvo odigrajte rezultat.

sections.title: Dokle zaista stiže?
sections.lede: Igra je brutalan test: kod koji radi, stotine grafika, razine zabavne dvadeset sati i šale koje pogađaju. Zato smo je napravili.

items.title: Kako je postavljeno
items.body:
Jedna osoba, tri tjedna, 580 commitova. Prava igra objavljena na pravom URL-u — ne prototip i ne demo snimka. Kampanja, beskonačno preživljavanje, stablo napretka, baza znanja, spremanje napretka i Android verzija.

Svaka odluka, slijepa ulica i vraćanje na staro zapisani su javno, dok su se događali.

items.title: Pošten odgovor
items.body:
Dalje nego što smo očekivali po količini — kod, grafika i razine dolazili su dovoljno brzo da opseg prestane biti ograničenje. Ne toliko daleko po ukusu. AI je znao reći može li se razina preživjeti, ali ne i je li dosadna.

Pokazalo se da je zanimljiv posao izrada alata koji čovjeku omogućuju brzu prosudbu — i zatim sama prosudba.

sections.title: Kod, grafika, razine, šale
sections.lede: Četiri različite vrste rezultata, četiri različita pipelinea — svaki pretvoren u ponovljiv proces, a ne u sretan prompt.

items.title: Sama igra
items.body:
Phaser 3 i TypeScript, oko 17.000 redaka u 54 modula: HUD s dvjema kamerama, matematika izometrijske projekcije, balistika projektila s opadanjem eksplozije po prstenovima polja, generiranje valova, sposobnosti bossova, sustav spremanja, proceduralni zvuk. Provjera tipova mora proći prije svakog pojedinog commita.

Nepromjenjiva pravila igre zapisana kao granice koje AI ne smije prijeći
Ravnoteža živi u podatkovnim datotekama, nikad u improviziranoj logici scene
Svaka mukotrpno naučena zamka zabilježena da se ne uči dvaput

items.title: 140 jedinstvenih putanja
items.body: Svaka razina dobiva vlastiti lijevak, generiran skriptom i zamrznut u build. Ulazi se izmjenjuju po sva četiri ruba, najmanji broj zavoja raste kako napredujete, a duljina je ograničena onime što to tržište može obraniti. Build se prekida ako ijedna razina padne ispod svog minimuma.

items.title: Više od 600 grafika, jedan pipeline
items.body:
Kule, korisnici, bossovi, ukrasi, polja, ikone sučelja i strip-kadrovi — sve generirano, pa im je pozadinu uklonio segmentacijski model, obrezano na sadržaj, zabilježeno i ugrađeno. Prompt, sjeme, rezolucija i model za svako generiranje stoje u JSON datoteci u repozitoriju, pa se svaka grafika može ponoviti ili vratiti.

Cijeli je postupak zapisan kao ponovno upotrebljiva vještina, a ne kao navika
Uklanjanje po boji zamijenjeno AI segmentacijom — prestalo je jesti tirkizni namještaj
Likovi u četiri smjera izvedeni iz jedne plošne slike, za nekoliko centi

items.title: Sedam svjetova, sedam skupova pravila
items.body: SAD, Europa, Kina, Afrika, Zemlja, svemir i odmetnici. Svako tržište nameće leću koja mijenja koliko dobar odgovor vrijedi — u Europi je privatnost kralj, uz obvezni sloj birokracije, a kineski vatrozid cenzurira jeftine odgovore. Iste kule, posve druga zagonetka.

items.title: Šale
items.body: Satirične udarne vijesti između razina, dobacivanja jedva prikrivenih tehnoloških titana kao bossova i kula-chatbot koja pri svakom pogotku izbaci novi samodopadni odgovor. Napisano prema specifikaciji tona, pa je čovjek prosijao one koje su zaista pogodile.

items.title: Zvuk bez zvučne biblioteke
items.body: Glazba i efekti sintetiziraju se u kodu umjesto da se uzorkuju — tema izbornika, klikovi sučelja, pogoci, eksplozije. Ništa za licenciranje, ništa za preuzimanje, a podešava se kao bilo koja druga podatkovna datoteka.

items.title: Radi na mobitelu
items.body: Zapakirano za Android, sa zaključanom orijentacijom i uvodnim zaslonom, nakon prolaza za performanse koji je otkrio da vrijeme po sličici troši HUD koji se iscrtava šezdeset puta u sekundi — a ne sama igra.

items.alt: Glavni izbornik Overserveda s načinima kampanja, preživljavanje, laboratorij za istraživanje, AGI laboratorij i baza znanja

sections.title: Bot koji igra igru
sections.lede: Podešavanje težine najsporija je petlja u razvoju igara, pa automatski igrač vrti stvarni pogon igre i javlja koliko je bio blizu porazu.

items.title: Igra kako treba
items.body: Nije glupa skripta. Kule postavlja po graničnoj pokrivenosti, koristeći stvarni doseg svake kule, teži poljima prema izlazu gdje se propuštanja doista događaju, čita leću tržišta pri kupnji, štedi valutu, gradi laboratorije i troši na nadogradnje — jer stvarni igrač radi sve to, a bot koji to ne radi past će na razinama koje su zapravo dobre.

items.title: Pronašao je stvarne greške
items.body: Puštanje kroz sve razine otkrilo je probleme koje nikakvo zurenje u tablicu ne bi: zid težine koji je nastao zbog omjera štete i cijene, a ne sirove štete, i bossove koji su prolazili neuslužni jer su kaskali iza vlastite pratnje, pa su kule gađale pratnju.

items.title: Onda ih je i osmislio
items.body: Kad je naučio dobro igrati, ručno podešavanje težine postalo je šum. Dizajn razina predan je njemu: svaki val raste dok ga bot jedva preživi. Svih 140 razina podesilo je nešto što ih je stvarno odigralo, a ne dizajner koji pogađa.

sections.title: Gdje je i dalje trebao čovjek
sections.lede: Neuspjesi su koristan dio ovog eksperimenta. Svaki je od njih u devlogu, jer referenca koja nabraja samo pobjede ne vrijedi čitati.

items.title: Uravnoteženo nije isto što i zabavno
items.body:
Bot je dokazao da se svaka razina može pobijediti. Nije mogao prepoznati da su neke dosadne. Ubačene su tri namjerno prejake kule i nije ih ni primijetio — ekonomija ih je progutala. „Može se preživjeti" mjerljivo je, „vrijedi dvadeset minuta Vaše večeri" nije.

Cijela značajka — nadogradnja kula po pojedinom svojstvu — objavljena je i izbrisana istog dana. Radila je besprijekorno i učinila igru gorom.

items.title: Vraćanje na staro bolje je od ponovnog generiranja
items.body:
Ponovno generiranje usklađenog skupa, jednu po jednu grafiku, potiho ga uništava — svaki render odluta u mjerilu, perspektivi i kadru dok se zbirka prestane slagati sama sa sobom. Skup kula tako je mjerljivo pogoršan pa je vraćen iz gita.

Cijeli je svijet izašao kao drugi svijet s crvenim filtrom preko njega. Plošna boja nije likovno vodstvo, a to je rekao samo čovjek koji ga je pogledao.

items.title: Što to zapravo znači za rad s klijentima
items.body: Lekcija nije „AI sada radi igre". Lekcija je da je generiranje jeftino, a prosudba nije, pa prednost leži u skeli oko generiranja: zabilježenom, ponovljivom pipelineu za grafiku; nepromjenjivim pravilima zapisanima ondje gdje se ne mogu zaboraviti; botu koji mjeri ono do čega Vam je stvarno stalo; i čovjeku čiji je cijeli posao odlučiti što je dobro. Overserved je mjesto gdje smo tu skelu izgradili i izmučili — u vlastito vrijeme, na projektu na kojem loša odluka ne stoji ništa.

sections.title: Dvadeset dva zapisa, s neuspjesima
sections.lede: Bilješke iz izrade — što je pokušano, što se slomilo, čemu nas je naučilo. Nekoliko primjera:

items.title: 4. srp
items.body: Prestao sam podešavati razine. Pustio sam bota da ih osmisli.

items.title: 2. srp
items.body: Usko grlo nije bila igra. Bila je to ploča s rezultatima.

items.title: 25. lip
items.body: Moja je tablica govorila da je igra uravnotežena. Nije mi mogla reći da je dosadna.

items.title: 25. lip
items.body: Napravio sam tri prejake kule. Bot ih nije ni primijetio.

items.title: 24. lip
items.body: Jedan redak prompta popravio je 96 mojih zgrada.

items.title: 23. lip
items.body: Napravio sam bota da odigra moju igru 140 puta. Našao je zid koji ja nisam vidio.

items.title: 19. lip
items.body: Iz plošne AI slike izvukao sam likove u 4 smjera, po dva centa komad.

items.title: 17. lip
items.body: Napravio sam nadogradnje kula po svojstvima i izbrisao ih do večere.
